repo_notes.content: Academic research project on metaheuristics for the 0/1 knapsack problem. Human authorship is the core rule: everything under knapsack-algorithms/src is written by hand without generative AI, while the surrounding ecosystem (knapsack-core, knapsack-bench, build, CI, docs) is developed with AI assistance. When documenting algorithms, describe what the code does as written, citing files and lines; state measured behaviour only when it comes from the bench output; leave assessments of correctness, fixes and improvement ideas out of the wiki, since they belong to the author. Java 25, Maven multi-module build with the Maven Wrapper. Code identifiers are English, project prose and CLI output are Spanish. The canonical documentation and experiment results are published with MkDocs on GitHub Pages at https://dmorfav.github.io/Knapsack/; link there for results instead of restating numbers.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce the project as a test bench for hand-written metaheuristics on the 0/1 knapsack problem, and state the human-authorship policy for algorithms

page_notes.content: Lead with the problem definition and the split between human-authored algorithms and the AI-assisted ecosystem, as stated in README.md.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Guide users through the Java 25 toolchain, the Maven Wrapper, running tests and running the bench with its command-line options

page_notes.content: Commands run from the repository root. Bench options are parsed in knapsack-bench Options.java: --instance, --seed, --max-evaluations, --max-seconds.

pages.title: System Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the three Maven modules, their dependency direction and how a solver is discovered, executed and validated

page_notes.content: Dependency direction: knapsack-algorithms depends only on knapsack-core; knapsack-bench depends on both. Solvers are discovered with java.util.ServiceLoader.

pages.title: Problem Model
pages.purpose: Document Instance, Item, Solution and Evaluation in knapsack-core

page_notes.content: Also cover the original model.Item and model.Knapsack classes, kept with their public API because the original algorithms import them.

pages.title: Solver Contract
pages.purpose: Document KnapsackSolver, SolverInfo, SolverContext, RunContext and Budget, including seeding, evaluation counting and budget exhaustion

page_notes.content: Explain the family/variant identity that allows several implementations of the same algorithm, and the steps to register a new solver.

pages.title: Instance Format
pages.purpose: Document the JSON instance format, validation rules and the instances shipped in the instances directory

page_notes.content: Source of truth is InstanceFiles.java. The legacy-* instances come from the original project and use capacity 100.

pages.title: Algorithms
pages.purpose: Overview of the hand-written metaheuristic implementations and how each is exposed to the bench

page_notes.content: Describe each algorithm as written. The original implementations run unmodified through legacy adapters, use Math.random and therefore ignore the run seed.

pages.title: Harmony Search Family
pages.purpose: Describe the Harmony Search, Improved Harmony Search and Discrete Binary Harmony Search implementations and their parameters

page_notes.content: Cover harmony memory, HMCR, PAR and bandwidth as implemented in knapsack-algorithms.

pages.title: Hill Climbing Family
pages.purpose: Describe the first-ascent and best-ascent hill climbing implementations

page_notes.content: Describe initial solution generation and neighbourhood exploration as implemented in knapsack-algorithms.

pages.title: Bench
pages.purpose: Document how the bench runs every discovered solver, validates its solution and reports profit, weight, evaluations and time

page_notes.content: Cover Main, SolverRun and the legacy adapters CountingKnapsack and LegacySolvers, which route every legacy model query through the counted, budgeted context.

pages.title: Development Workflow
pages.purpose: Document the build configuration, test suites, continuous integration and the authorship guardrails

page_notes.content: Include the Maven enforcer rules, JaCoCo coverage, the GitHub Actions workflows build.yml and qa.yml, and the Claude Code hooks in .claude/hooks that protect knapsack-algorithms/src and reserve commits for the author.
